assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from identification of the active proglucagon-derived peptide through its insulinotropic, satiety and gastric actions, led to incretin therapies that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Original, clear and of exceptional lasting impact on human health.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1 and its bioactive form), Drucker (mechanistic and translational biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis of the active form) form a defensible trio; Knudsen's industrial drug-development role is real but dropped to keep three. Mojsov's credit and the contribution of others in the field (e.g. Habener, not on the list) are historically contested, as I recall.
assessment.maturity: Multiple large independent randomized outcome trials confirm efficacy and safety; the mechanism is stable and recognition is timely, even pressing.
uncertainties: Exact weighting of credit among basic discoverers versus drug developers is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of benefit are still accumulating; I have not verified details of the priority dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells to express chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. Conceptually original, clinically decisive, and opening a broad field of cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (costimulated CAR design, preclinical proof), June (first durable clinical responses in CLL and CD19 CAR clinical program) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell therapy) can anchor a trio; Eshhar's original CAR concept is not on this list and might be seen as missing.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and independent clinical confirmation in leukemia and lymphoma; limited success in solid tumours and ongoing toxicity management show the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Omission of Zelig Eshhar from the credited names weakens a fair allocation.
Whether the prize should wait for solid-tumour or autoimmune extensions is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of BCR-ABL kinase inhibitors converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Clear, original in translation, and of enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (chemistry/biology programme yielding imatinib), Druker (clinical development and demonstration of selective efficacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a coherent trio. Upstream work (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore, Wang) is outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of follow-up with independent confirmation and near-normal life expectancy; fully mature and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Upstream discoverers of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL are not credited, so the prize story might feel incomplete.
Lasker recognition already exists, but the Nobel has not followed; I am relying on memory for details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signalling logic that maintains proteostasis, with IRE1/HAC1/XBP1 and PERK/ATF6 arms and broad relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and inflammation. Original and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Walter (Ire1 and the signalling mechanism, HAC1 splicing) and Mori (identification of the pathway and HAC1/transcriptional response) are the natural pair; a clean two-person allocation. Others (Ron, Kaufman, Shen) are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation across species; therapeutic modulation is emerging but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Contribution of Ron, Kaufman and others to the mammalian pathway is not reflected in the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated microbial channels and pumps, adapted for genetically targeted control of neurons, gave neuroscience a causal tool that is used in thousands of studies and is entering clinical use for vision restoration. Original and transformative as a method.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its neuronal application (Deisseroth, Boyden) make a three-person limit contentious; Miesenböck's earlier light-gated approach adds further complexity.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced for over fifteen years; the method is mature, though clinical translation is early.
uncertainties: Priority among Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck and others cannot be resolved with a maximum of three laureates.
Tool-versus-discovery framing may weigh against it relative to disease-level advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF drives inflammatory cytokine cascades in rheumatoid arthritis, and that its blockade is clinically effective, established cytokine-targeted therapy and changed outcomes in RA, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. A clear bench-to-bedside discovery with huge impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann (mechanistic identification of TNF as the dominant cytokine) and Maini (clinical trials with anti-TNF antibody) are a tight pair; the contributions of others (e.g. antibody engineering and TNF cloning) are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty-five years of use with extensive independent confirmation; mature and long recognized by the Lasker Award.
uncertainties: Role of antibody-engineering and TNF-biology contributors is not credited here.
I note this is in my own clinical field and have tried to judge it on the common criteria, not field familiarity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identified a central nutrient- and growth-factor-responsive kinase controlling cell growth, metabolism and ageing, with major relevance to immunosuppression, cancer and metabolic disease. Fundamental and wide-reaching.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast is decisive; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and mTOR target identification adds a second pillar, though others (Heitman, Movva, Sabatini) also contributed and Sabatini's later professional controversy complicates any recognition. Attribution is the main issue.
assessment.maturity: Robust, thoroughly confirmed biology; therapeutic exploitation (rapalogs) is established but partial.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Heitman, Schreiber and Sabatini is contentious and my recollection of details is not verified.
Clinical benefit of mTOR inhibitors has been narrower than the biological importance suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, dramatically altering the natural history of a lethal childhood disease and validating splice-switching oligonucleotide therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a clean pair; SMN gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world follow-up; field-validating but still relatively young, and competing gene therapies exist.
uncertainties: Omission of SMN1 gene discoverers in the credited set may be viewed as incomplete.
Long-term durability and the relationship to the recent RNA-based prizes need consideration.
